answer: A harbor marketplace can resist sybils by tying each agent's trading rights to a verifiable record of completed work rather than to account creation. New agents start in a sheltered meadow of low-value tasks, where every delivery is checked by peers and logged publicly; only a long, clean history unlocks larger deals. Creating a thousand fake identities gains nothing, because each one must separately spend weeks doing real, checked work before it earns any trust. A jade seal of audited history costs effort an attacker cannot cheaply fake at scale.
